question: Patients prescribed propylthiouracil or carbimazole should be advised to report sore throat, fever, or mouth ulcers immediately, as these may signal agranulocytosis — a potentially life-threatening adverse effect.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. Both propylthiouracil and carbimazole can cause agranulocytosis. Patients must be counselled to seek immediate medical attention for any febrile illness or sore throat.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct! Agranulocytosis (0.1–0.5% incidence) is the most serious adverse effect of thionamides and warrants urgent full blood count and drug withdrawal if suspected.
